root: ^Brumild: Wipe your boots on the rug, did you? Good! No muddy footprints in my house, thanks. Sit yourself down and have a pickle—family recipe.

c-0: ^Brumild: Name’s Brumild Copperpot. Born and raised under the old mountain, where the stones rumble louder than my husband’s snoring. He’s a retired engineer—built half the bridges in town before his hands started shaking.
^ We got married after he beat my father at chess. Father says he lost because he mistook a pawn for the king, but I think he just wanted me married off to someone smart.
^Brumild: Our place is small, but it’s full of laughter, music, and the smell of fresh bread. We’re not much for gold and glitter—give me a warm hearth and a good story any day.

s0: ^That skeleton in the church sings better than me.
s1: ^Thought you were the librarian for a second—got a pile of overdue books. What? Stories matter, you know.
s2: ^The clothier’s daughter is learning her dad’s trade. She could sell snow to a snowman, that one. Armor at double the price, and folks still buy it!
s3: ^Festival’s coming up, mark my words. I’m pickling twice as much—never know who’ll show up hungry.

c-2: ^Brumild: Ah, my pickles! Each jar’s got a story. Some’ll set your tongue on fire, some’ll make you pucker. Gran taught me everything—try the beetroot if you’re brave, or the garlic dill if you want a kick!
